## TL;DR
`repoos restart` restarts this repo's server whether it is a RepoOS service, an external launchd/systemd supervisor (including system-domain LaunchDaemons, the Kamrai case) or hand-run, and keeps the old serve flags. This round fixes review pass 7: flags were read from a pid that was already dead.

## Work and rationale
- `src/core/server-restart.ts`: the serve flags are now resolved once, before the stop (while `ps` can still read the old pid's command line), and that value is used for the respawn and for both manual commands (spawn failure and wait failure). Before, the fallback to `extractServeFlagsFromCommand(readProcessCommand(pid))` ran after `waitPidGone`, so any server whose lock predates `serveFlags`, or that was found through the registry, respawned without `--preview-overrides`, `--quiet` and `--no-tailscale-https`.
- Test in `src/core/server-restart.test.ts`: a registry-located server with no lock flags, where the flags are only readable while the pid is alive; the respawn must still receive them.
- Earlier rounds on the branch: system-domain `launchctl print`, `managed` kind, lock-based pid ownership proof for installed RepoOS servers, managed-port match, shutdown warning, accurate failure guidance, down-state hint.

## Approaches tried
Resolving the flags into the `LocatedServer` before the stop would change the locator contract; resolving them inside `restartRepoServer` before the signal fixes every use with one local value.

## Challenges and blockers
Not verified live: a non-sudo KeepAlive LaunchDaemon respawn and `launchctl print system` pid rows for a non-root user; both are covered by fixtures.

## Key learnings
Read all process state before signalling the process.
